metaDescription: Six countertop crushed and nugget ice makers compared on first-batch time, tank design, daily output and how auger machines differ from cube crushers.
expertTake: The Euhomy 2026 upgraded nugget maker is the crushed-ice pick for most kitchens, with a dual-pump design and a claimed 5 to 7 minute first batch. The Silonn 44 lb with a front pull-out tank is the one for heavy daily use. Skip any machine marketed as a crusher if you want soft pellets, because crushed ice from a blender is jagged and melts fast, while nugget ice is made soft.
introParagraphs: Crushed ice, pebble ice, sonic ice and nugget ice all describe the same thing in practice: small, soft, chewable pellets that cool a drink fast and soak up its flavor. A countertop machine makes them by scraping a frozen layer off a chilled cylinder and compressing the shavings.

That process explains the trade-offs. An auger machine is heavier and louder than a cube maker, it uses a proper compressor, and it needs descaling because scale on the cylinder slows the auger. We rank the field on how quickly each makes its first batch, how it handles water and what it asks of you to keep it healthy.

products.name: Euhomy 2026 upgraded countertop nugget ice maker, 35 lb, dual pump
products.description:
Euhomy's upgraded model adds a dual-pump layout and quotes a first batch in about five to seven minutes, a faster start than most nugget machines. Two pumps let the machine move water through its circuit and drain cleaning water more thoroughly, which helps both ice production and the self-cleaning routine.

What comes out is the soft, crunchy nugget that people call sonic or crushed, and a 35 pound daily figure covers a household's daily drinks. The maker's own advice is worth noting: after a deep clean with descaler, run two or three self-cleaning cycles with fresh water and discard the first batch or two of ice.

Against the 44 lb Euhomy it makes less but starts faster. As with all auger machines it is louder than a cube maker, so place it where the hum is tolerable, keep vents clear and descale every month or two.
products.bestFor: Most kitchens that want chewable ice with a quick first batch.
pros: First batch in about 5 to 7 minutes
Dual-pump design aids cleaning and flow
cons: 35 lb per day is a best-case figure

products.name: Silonn countertop nugget ice maker, 44 lb, front pull-out tank
products.description:
The Silonn's headline feature is access: a front pull-out water tank and a detachable ice basket mean you can refill and clean without turning the machine around on the counter. For a heavy-use household that is a real daily convenience, and the 44 pound output is the highest in this group.

The maker says soft chewable ice arrives in about ten minutes, slower than the Euhomy's first batch, which is the trade for the bigger output. The pebble ice it makes is the same soft, compacted type as the other machines here.

Against the Euhomy it makes more and is easier to service, but starts later. Pull the tank and rinse it regularly, descale the cylinder every month or two, and keep clearance around the vents.
products.bestFor: Heavy daily users who want easy access to the tank and basket.
pros: Quoted 44 lb per day is the highest here
Front pull-out tank is easy to refill
cons: Slower first batch at about 10 minutes

products.name: Silonn countertop nugget ice maker with carry handle, 36 lb, 5 min
products.description:
Silonn pitches this as a cost-effective, fast nugget maker, with first ice in about five minutes and a daily output of 36 pounds. The carry handle makes it easy to move, which matters because auger machines are heavy for a countertop appliance.

The five-minute figure is a maker claim for the first batch from a cold start, and it is the fastest in this group alongside the upgraded Euhomy. Expect the same soft restaurant-style nugget that cools a drink quickly and holds flavor. A 36 pound daily output sits in the middle of the range.

Compared with the 44 lb Silonn it is faster and smaller. Place it where the compressor can breathe, descale regularly and let the machine dry if it will sit idle for days.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a quick first batch and a handle.
pros: First ice in about 5 minutes by claim
cons: Less access than a front pull-out tank

products.name: Euhomy nugget ice maker countertop, 44 lb, 7 to 10 min, black
products.description:
This black Euhomy delivers 44 pounds a day and ships with a scoop and basket, claiming soft chewable ice in seven to ten minutes. It matches the Silonn 44 lb on output and brings the Euhomy name to a heavy-use machine.

The seven to ten minute range is the maker's own spread, which tells you the real figure depends on room and water temperature. A self-cleaning function handles the routine flush. The black finish is a styling choice that hides fingerprints on a countertop.

Against the upgraded Euhomy 35 lb it makes more and starts later and lacks the dual pump. Keep the vents clear, descale on schedule and drain the tank if the machine will sit unused.
products.bestFor: Heavy users who want a branded 44 lb machine with accessories included.
cons: Start time ranges from 7 to 10 minutes

products.name: Kismile nugget ice maker countertop, 35 lb, stainless steel, 1.1L tank
products.description:
Kismile's machine is a stainless steel portable nugget maker with a 1.1 liter tank and a daily output of 35 pounds. The maker says a five second press of the power button starts the cleaning cycle, a simple interface for a task that most owners skip.

The 1.1 liter tank is the smallest in this group, so the machine needs refilling more often, and that matters at parties. A stainless body feels solid and resists scratches. It is a lesser-known brand, so parts and support are thinner than the big names.

Against the Euhomy it matches the output with a smaller tank and a one-press clean. Descale regularly, keep clearance around the vents and watch the tank level.
products.bestFor: Small households that want a stainless body and easy cleaning.

products.name: Euhomy nugget ice maker with handle, 34 lb, 6 min, removable cover
products.description:
A removable top cover is the feature that sets this Euhomy apart: you can lift the lid off and wipe the inside of the bin without fighting a hinge, which makes real cleaning easier. The maker claims first ice in as little as six minutes and 34 pounds a day.

It makes small, airy pellet ice that cools drinks quickly, and a carry handle lets you move the machine. An auto-cleaning cycle handles the routine flush, though scale on the cylinder still needs descaling.

Compared with the 44 lb Euhomy it makes less and starts faster. Wipe the bin with the cover off every couple of weeks, descale monthly and keep clearance on all sides.
products.bestFor: Owners who want an easy-to-wipe bin.
pros: Removable top cover for easy cleaning
First ice in as little as 6 minutes
cons: 34 lb per day is middle of the range

buyingCriteria.explanation: A true nugget maker scrapes a frozen layer off a cold cylinder with an auger and compresses it, producing soft, airy pellets. A crusher smashes ordinary cubes into jagged pieces that melt fast. All six machines here are auger makers, which is why they are heavier and pricier than cube makers. If you want crushed ice for a blender, you may not need a dedicated machine.

Claimed first-batch times run from about 5 minutes on the Silonn 36 lb and the upgraded Euhomy to about 10 minutes on the Silonn 44 lb. A faster start matters for spur-of-the-moment drinks, but daily output matters more for a household that drinks all day. Trade a few minutes for a higher output if you use a lot of ice. Remember too that the first-batch figure is a cold-start number, and later cycles run steadily, so the difference of a few minutes disappears once the machine is warm and the bin is filling.

A front pull-out tank like Silonn's 44 lb makes refilling easy, and a 1.1 liter tank like Kismile's means more trips to the sink. The tank size sets how long the machine can run unattended. Consider how often you will refill and whether the tank is easy to reach. A tank that has to be lifted out the back of a machine against a wall will be refilled less often, and the machine will sit empty more than you would like.

Auger machines add a grinding sound to the compressor hum, louder than a cube maker. Place the machine away from a bedroom, on a solid counter, with several inches of clearance. A cabinet that traps heat raises the noise and cuts output.

Self-cleaning cycles, which every machine here lists, flush the reservoir but do not remove mineral scale from the cylinder. Scale slows the auger and cuts output. Plan a monthly or bimonthly descale with citric acid, and run clean water cycles afterward as the maker advises.

Hard water scales an auger machine faster than a cube maker, and the scale is on the part that matters most. Filtered or distilled water slows the buildup. If you notice the ice turning cloudy or the machine slowing, descale before it becomes a repair.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ice type
howWeEvaluated.description: We confirmed each machine is an auger nugget maker, not a cube crusher. All six qualified. We noted where marketing used the word crushed for a pellet ice.

howWeEvaluated.title: Start and output
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared first-batch claims, from about 5 minutes to 10, and daily output from 34 to 44 pounds. Faster starts scored for convenience. Higher output scored for heavy use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Access and cleaning
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at pull-out tanks, detachable baskets and removable covers. Machines that are easy to reach scored higher. We noted that none removes scale automatically.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and footprint
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered auger noise and body size, including handles and weight. Quieter placement mattered. Smaller footprints scored for small kitchens.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at brand support, clear maintenance advice and accessories. The Euhomy's cleaning guidance was a plus. Lesser-known brands were credited for price but marked for support.

maintenance.why: Scale slows the auger and cuts output. Citric acid or a maker-approved descaler restores it.
Residue left behind tastes bad. The maker advises two or three clean cycles and discarding early ice, and a taste test of the first fresh batch is the simplest way to know the rinse worked.
A warm, wet bin grows biofilm. A removable cover makes this a quick job, and a dilute vinegar or mild sanitizer wipe, followed by a rinse, keeps the surfaces clean without leaving a smell.

Standing water grows slime. Drain and dry it if the machine will sit unused. Leave the cover off for a day so air can reach the corners, and give the machine a clean cycle with fresh water before the first use after a long break.

A dusty condenser starves the compressor of air, so the crushed ice machine gets louder and makes less. A soft brush or a vacuum with a brush head clears the grille, and a quick look behind the machine tells you whether it is pushed too close to the wall.

faq.q: Are crushed ice makers different from nugget ice makers?
faq.a: Usually they are the same machine. Nugget, pebble, sonic and crushed all describe soft compacted pellets from an auger maker. A cube crusher is a different product, and it makes jagged shards that melt quickly rather than airy pellets. Check the listing for the words auger, nugget or pebble, and be wary of one that only says crushes ice.

faq.q: Why is nugget ice so popular?
faq.a: It is soft and chewable, and it absorbs the flavor of the drink around it. It also cools a drink quickly because of its large surface area. The pellets are compacted from thin layers, so they are airy and crunch easily, and that structure is also why they melt faster than a solid cube of the same size.

faq.q: How loud is a crushed ice maker?
faq.a: Louder than a cube maker, with a compressor hum and an auger grind. Place it away from a bedroom and leave vent clearance. A rubber mat under the feet reduces the vibration that travels through a hollow counter, and a quiet moment between cycles is normal, because the compressor and auger rest when the bin is full.

faq.q: Do I need to descale it?
faq.a: Yes, every month or two. Scale on the cylinder slows the auger. Self-cleaning cycles do not remove it.

You can, but hard water scales faster. Filtered or distilled water slows the buildup and keeps the ice cleaner. In a soft-water home tap water is fine, and a quick test strip from a hardware store tells you which camp you are in before you commit to buying water.

faq.q: Does the ice stay frozen in the machine?
faq.a: No. The bin is not a freezer, so melt water drains back to the reservoir. Use the ice fresh or bag and freeze it. Nugget ice clumps when it sits wet, so a freezer bag with the air pressed out holds it better than an open bowl, and a quick shake breaks up the clumps.
